definitions.explanation: A language designated for use in government, law, and official business of a country or region. A country may have one or multiple official languages.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}は{公用語|こうようご}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: English is one of the official languages.

examples.japanese: この{国|くに}には{公用語|こうようご}が{四|よっ}つある。
examples.english: This country has four official languages.

examples.japanese: {国連|こくれん}の{公用語|こうようご}は{英語|えいご}、{仏語|ふつご}、{中国語|ちゅうごくご}など{六|ろく}つある。
examples.english: The United Nations has six official languages, including English, French, and Chinese.

notes:
Japan has no legally designated {公用語|こうようご} — Japanese is the de facto national language but is not formally codified as the official language in the constitution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公用語|こうようご}に{指定|してい}する (designate as an official language)
- {公用語|こうようご}として{使|つか}われる (be used as an official language)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公用語|こうようご}: official language (legally designated for government use)
- {国語|こくご}: national language (the language of a nation, also the school subject)
- {母語|ぼご}: mother tongue, native language
